docs.title: MSFLib FastAPI Documentation
docs.text:
MSFLib FastAPI is a modular backend framework built around a shared core package and a family of independently installable modules. The monorepo is designed for teams that want a secure, scoped, and extensible FastAPI foundation without forcing every application to adopt every feature.

This documentation focuses on the public packages shipped in this repository and the patterns used to integrate them into a host application.

docs.title: Repository structure
docs.text:
The core repo is organized around a shared runtime and optional feature modules:

  • core/ — shared configuration, security, event bus, database, scope, and policy primitives
  • modules/account — account and profile lifecycle
  • modules/auth — auth, JWT tokens, password reset, Google OAuth
  • modules/ai_core — LLM, embeddings, vector store, and agent/tool plumbing
  • modules/ai_api — user-facing AI endpoints and transport adapters
  • modules/documents — upload, extraction, ingestion, and indexing flow
  • modules/workspaces — workspace lifecycle and workspace-aware profile access
  • modules/workspace_config — tenant/workspace/user tiered config storage
  • modules/notifications — in-app and broadcast notifications
  • modules/workspace_notifications — workspace-scoped notification flows
  • modules/ingestion — shared job queue and ingestion execution pipeline
  • modules/knowledge — knowledge graph and retrieval-oriented domain model

docs.title: Recommended installation pattern
docs.text:
Use Poetry and install only the modules your app needs.

[tool.poetry.dependencies]
python = ">=3.10,<4.0"
msflib = { git = "https://github.com/msflib/fastapi.git", subdirectory = "core", rev = "dev" }
msflib-account = { git = "https://github.com/msflib/fastapi.git", subdirectory = "modules/account", rev = "dev" }
msflib-auth = { git = "https://github.com/msflib/fastapi.git", subdirectory = "modules/auth", rev = "dev" }
msflib-workspaces = { git = "https://github.com/msflib/fastapi.git", subdirectory = "modules/workspaces", rev = "dev" }

docs.title: Quick start
docs.text:
from fastapi import FastAPI

from msflib.auth.router import router as auth_router
from msflib.account.router import account_router, profile_router
from msflib.workspaces.router import router as workspaces_router

app = FastAPI()

app.include_router(auth_router(prefix="/auth"))
app.include_router(account_router(prefix="/account"))
app.include_router(profile_router(prefix="/profiles"))
app.include_router(workspaces_router(prefix="/workspaces"))

docs.title: Module guide
docs.text: Module Purpose Documentation Core Config, policy, database, security, scope, event bus core.md Account Account and profile management account.md Auth JWT auth, logout, reset, OAuth auth.md AI Core LLM, embeddings, vectors, providers ai_core.md Workspaces Workspace lifecycle and membership workspaces.md Workspace Config Tiered config persistence across tenant/workspace/user workspace_config.md Notifications In-app and broadcast notifications notifications.md Workspace Notifications Workspace-scoped notification routes workspace_notifications.md Documents Upload, extraction, indexing documents.md Ingestion Shared job queue and pipeline execution ingestion.md Knowledge Knowledge graph, semantics, and agent grounding knowledge.md AI API Search, ask, and agent APIs ai_api.md

docs.title: Typical application flow
docs.text:
Most projects follow a layered setup:

  1. Install msflib core.
  2. Add account and auth to manage identity.
  3. Add workspaces and workspace_config for organization and scoped settings.
  4. Add ai_core and ai_api when building AI features.
  5. Add documents, ingestion, and knowledge when implementing retrieval pipelines.
  6. Wire in notifications or workspace_notifications for product events and user messaging.

docs.title: Development notes
docs.text:
• Settings are organized with namespace-scoped configuration and tier precedence.
  • Core features are shared across modules via SettingsBase, ModuleSettingsBase, and scoped config resolution.
  • Authentication and workspace-based authorization rely on dependency factories rather than one-off route logic.
  • The repo favors modular installation, not a single monolithic server package.

docs.title: Next steps
docs.text: Start with the core and auth docs, then move into workspaces and account flows before integrating AI and document ingestion.

docs.title: Account Module
docs.text: The Account module provides account and profile management for MSFLib-based FastAPI projects. It covers self-service registration, profile lifecycle, admin management, and schema-based validation patterns that are easy to override in downstream applications.

docs.title: What it provides
docs.text:
• Current-account and profile endpoints
  • Open registration support with a single configurable public route
  • Admin account management routes
  • Optional nested profile creation during signup
  • Action classes such as AccountAction and ProfileAction
  • Custom schema support for account-creation validation

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
[tool.poetry.dependencies]
msflib = { git = "https://github.com/msflib/fastapi.git", subdirectory = "core", rev = "dev" }
msflib-account = { git = "https://github.com/msflib/fastapi.git", subdirectory = "modules/account", rev = "dev" }

docs.title: Router wiring
docs.text:
from fastapi import FastAPI
from msflib.account.router import account_router, account_admin_router, profile_router

app = FastAPI()

app.include_router(
    account_router(
        get_session=get_session,
        get_current_account=get_current_account,
        settings=settings,
        account_type=Account,
        profile_type=Profile,
    )
)

app.include_router(
    account_admin_router(
        get_session=get_session,
        role_check=role_check,
        settings=settings,
        account_type=Account,
        profile_type=Profile,
    )
)

app.include_router(
    profile_router(
        get_session=get_session,
        get_current_account=get_current_account,
        get_current_active_account=get_current_active_account,
        settings=settings,
        account_type=Account,
        profile_type=Profile,
    )
)

docs.title: Public API surface
docs.text: Name Signature Params Returns Description account_router account_router(...) session deps, current account dep, settings, types FastAPI router Registers account and self-service profile endpoints account_admin_router account_admin_router(...) admin role check, settings, account/profile types FastAPI router Registers admin-only account management routes profile_router profile_router(...) session deps, current account deps, settings FastAPI router Exposes profile CRUD and avatar upload routes AccountAction AccountAction[...] settings, profile_action, custom schema hooks action instance Service layer for account lifecycle ProfileAction ProfileAction[...] settings action instance Service layer for profile-specific logic

docs.title: User routes
docs.text:
• GET /account/me — current authenticated account
  • PUT /account/me — update current account
  • POST /account/open — optional public registration route
  • POST /account/verify-availability — check email/username/phone availability

docs.title: Admin routes
docs.text:
• GET /admin/accounts — list accounts
  • POST /admin/accounts — create account
  • GET /admin/accounts/{account_id} — fetch single account
  • PUT /admin/accounts/{account_id} — update account

docs.title: Profile routes
docs.text:
• GET /profiles — current profile
  • GET /profiles/{account_id} — profile by account id
  • POST /profiles — create or upsert profile
  • PUT /profiles — update current profile
  • PUT /profiles/avatar — upload avatar

docs.title: Custom validation
docs.text:
The module supports custom account-creation schemas via account_create_type without changing the route shape.

from myapp.schemas import CustomAccountCreate

app.include_router(
    account_router(
        get_session=get_session,
        get_current_account=get_current_account,
        settings=settings,
        account_type=Account,
        profile_type=Profile,
        account_create_type=CustomAccountCreate,
    )
)

This is especially useful when you need extra signup fields such as company, locale, or compliance metadata.

docs.title: Example: open registration
docs.text:
app.include_router(
    account_router(
        get_session=get_session,
        get_current_account=get_current_account,
        settings=settings,
        account_type=Account,
        profile_type=Profile,
        open_registration_path="/signup",
    )
)

With a default /account prefix, this creates POST /account/signup.

docs.title: Settings
docs.text:
Account settings are read under the ACCOUNT namespace. Typical keys include:

  • USERS_OPEN_REGISTRATION
  • OPEN_REGISTRATION_PATH
  • FIRST_SUPERUSER
  • FIRST_SUPERUSER_PASSWORD
  • EMAIL_TEST_ACCOUNT

docs.title: Error handling and troubleshooting
docs.text:
• Invalid signup payloads return validation errors before the account is created.
  • If profile creation is enabled with a custom schema, make sure the related ProfileAction is passed correctly.
  • If open registration is disabled, POST /account/open will not be available.

docs.title: Testing
docs.text: ./scripts/test.sh modules/account/msflib/account/tests

docs.title: AI API Module
docs.text: The AI API module exposes user-facing routes for search, Q&A, and agent-style workflow interactions built on the shared AI Core runtime.

docs.title: What it provides
docs.text:
• Search endpoint for retrieval over configured vector stores
  • Ask endpoint for retrieval-augmented responses
  • Agent status and agent ask endpoints
  • Response protocol support for different client expectations
  • Scoped routing based on account and workspace context

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
[tool.poetry.dependencies]
msflib = { git = "https://github.com/msflib/fastapi.git", subdirectory = "core", rev = "dev" }
msflib-ai-api = { git = "https://github.com/msflib/fastapi.git", subdirectory = "modules/ai_api", rev = "dev" }

docs.title: Example: mount the router
docs.text:
from fastapi import FastAPI
from msflib.ai_api.router import router as ai_router

app = FastAPI()
app.include_router(ai_router(prefix="/api/v1/ai"))

docs.title: Public API surface
docs.text: Name Signature Params Returns Description router router(...) session, account/workspace deps, settings FastAPI router Main AI transport routes create_llm_router create_llm_router(...) model and deps router Creates routable LLM ask endpoints create_agent_router create_agent_router(...) agent config and deps router Creates agent-aware ask endpoints

docs.title: Routes
docs.text:
• POST /ai/search — retrieval and hit lookup
  • POST /ai/ask — grounded answer generation
  • GET /ai/status — service status
  • GET /ai/protocols — supported response protocols
  • GET /ai/agent/status — agent runtime status
  • POST /ai/agent/ask — agent-based question answering
  • POST /ai/agent/ask/stream — streaming agent response

docs.title: Search
docs.text:
POST /api/v1/ai/search
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "query": "replace retrieval",
  "k": 3
}

docs.title: Ask
docs.text:
POST /api/v1/ai/ask
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "question": "What does the latest content mention?",
  "k": 2
}

docs.title: Protocol handling
docs.text: The ask endpoint supports response protocols such as the default native protocol or OpenAI-style envelopes. The X-AI-Protocol header can override the default when needed.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
• Requests without workspace context may fail validation when workspace-scoped retrieval is required.
  • Unsupported protocols return a client error.
  • Provider selection depends on the underlying AI Core registry and task binding configuration.

docs.title: AI Core Module
docs.text: The AI Core module provides the shared infrastructure for LLM, embeddings, vector search, provider registry, and prompt/tool orchestration across MSFLib services.

docs.title: What it provides
docs.text:
• Unified LLM and embeddings factories
  • Provider registry abstractions for many LangChain backends
  • Vector store abstractions and scoped retrieval helpers
  • Request rate limiting and usage tracking
  • Long-term memory and checkpoint support for agent workflows
  • Tool factories for calculators, search, and retrieval helpers

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
[tool.poetry.dependencies]
msflib = { git = "https://github.com/msflib/fastapi.git", subdirectory = "core", rev = "dev" }
msflib-ai-core = { git = "https://github.com/msflib/fastapi.git", subdirectory = "modules/ai_core", rev = "dev" }

Optional provider extras can be added later depending on your LLM stack.

docs.title: Example: create an LLM and embedding model
docs.text:
from msflib.ai_core.config import AICoreSettings
from msflib.ai_core.providers import get_llm, get_embeddings

settings = AICoreSettings(
    LLM_PROVIDER="openai",
    LLM_MODEL="gpt-4o-mini",
    LLM_API_KEY="sk-...",
    EMBEDDING_PROVIDER="openai",
    EMBEDDING_MODEL="text-embedding-3-small",
    EMBEDDING_API_KEY="sk-...",
)

llm = get_llm(settings)
embeddings = get_embeddings(settings)

docs.title: Public API surface
docs.text: Name Signature Params Returns Description get_llm get_llm(settings) AI core settings LLM instance Builds a configured chat model get_embeddings get_embeddings(settings) AI core settings embedding model Builds an embedding model register_provider_type register_provider_type(...) provider metadata None Adds a new provider to the registry get_provider_type_registry get_provider_type_registry() none registry Lists and resolves available providers get_vector_store get_vector_store(...) backend config store interface Resolves the configured vector backend

docs.title: Retrieval-augmented workflow
docs.text:
from msflib.ai_core.providers import get_llm

llm = get_llm(settings)
response = llm.invoke("Summarize the latest product notes for customer support.")
print(response)

docs.title: Vector-based search
docs.text:
from msflib.ai_core.providers import get_embeddings

embeddings = get_embeddings(settings)
vector = embeddings.embed_query("How do I reset my workspace password?")

docs.title: Configuration and environment variables
docs.text:
Typical values include:

  • AI_CORE__LLM_PROVIDER
  • AI_CORE__LLM_MODEL
  • AI_CORE__LLM_API_KEY
  • AI_CORE__EMBEDDING_PROVIDER
  • AI_CORE__EMBEDDING_MODEL
  • AI_CORE__EMBEDDING_API_KEY

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
• Missing provider packages raise actionable import errors telling you which extra to install.
  • Unsupported embedding and LLM provider combinations fail fast during validation.
  • Vector store backend mismatches usually mean the configured backend is not installed or not initialized.

docs.title: Auth Module
docs.text: The Auth module handles authentication, JWT lifecycle, password recovery, logout, and the reusable dependency factories used to secure routes in a FastAPI app.

docs.title: What it provides
docs.text:
• Login and access-token issuance
  • Logout with token revocation
  • Password recovery and reset flow
  • Optional Google OAuth login/callback
  • Resource-scoped dependency factories for account and workspace checks

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
[tool.poetry.dependencies]
msflib = { git = "https://github.com/msflib/fastapi.git", subdirectory = "core", rev = "dev" }
msflib-auth = { git = "https://github.com/msflib/fastapi.git", subdirectory = "modules/auth", rev = "dev" }

docs.title: Router wiring
docs.text:
from fastapi import FastAPI
from msflib.auth.router import router as auth_router

app = FastAPI()

app.include_router(
    auth_router(
        get_session=get_session,
        get_keystore=get_keystore,
        get_current_account=account_deps.get_current_account,
        account_type=Account,
        account_read_type=AccountRead,
        settings=settings,
        prefix="/auth",
    )
)

docs.title: Dependency factories
docs.text:
The module exposes helpers for account-level and workspace-level auth dependencies.

from msflib.auth.deps import get_account_dependencies, get_user_dependencies
from msflib.auth.resolvers import PathParameterResolver

account_deps = get_account_dependencies(
    AccountModel=Account,
    oauth_token_url="/api/v1/auth/login",
    secret_key=settings.SECRET_KEY,
    session_dep=get_session,
    keystore_dep=get_keystore,
)

user_deps = get_user_dependencies(
    UserModel=WorkspaceUser,
    WorkspaceModel=Workspace,
    session_dep=get_session,
    account_dependencies=account_deps,
    workspace_resolver=PathParameterResolver(),
)

These factories allow apps to centralize access checks instead of duplicating logic in each endpoint.

docs.title: Public API surface
docs.text: Name Signature Params Returns Description auth_router auth_router(...) session dep, keystore dep, current account dep, settings FastAPI router Handles login, reset, OAuth, and logout endpoints get_account_dependencies get_account_dependencies(...) AccountModel, secret_key, session/keystore deps dependency namespace Builds account-level auth dependencies get_user_dependencies get_user_dependencies(...) UserModel, WorkspaceModel, account dependencies dependency namespace Builds workspace-aware auth dependencies PathParameterResolver PathParameterResolver() none resolver Resolves workspace context from route params

docs.title: Routes
docs.text:
• POST /auth/login — issue an access token
  • POST /auth/password-recovery — request a password reset
  • POST /auth/verify-token — validate a token or recovery reference
  • POST /auth/reset-password — complete password reset
  • DELETE /auth/logout — revoke session token
  • GET /auth/google/login — Google OAuth start flow
  • POST /auth/google/callback — Google OAuth callback

docs.title: OAuth payload validation
docs.text:
When Google OAuth is enabled, the module supports a typed payload model for callback validation.

from pydantic import BaseModel

class GoogleAuthPayload(BaseModel):
    workspace_id: str
    organization_id: str | None = None

Then pass it to the router:

app.include_router(
    auth_router(
        get_session=get_session,
        get_keystore=get_keystore,
        get_current_account=account_deps.get_current_account,
        account_type=Account,
        account_read_type=AccountRead,
        settings=settings,
        auth_payload_type=GoogleAuthPayload,
    )
)

docs.title: Example: login flow
docs.text:
from msflib.auth.deps import get_account_dependencies

account_deps = get_account_dependencies(
    AccountModel=Account,
    oauth_token_url="/auth/login",
    secret_key=settings.SECRET_KEY,
    session_dep=get_session,
    keystore_dep=get_keystore,
)

# downstream app can then use account_deps.get_current_account in Depends(...)

docs.title: Settings
docs.text:
Auth settings live under the AUTH namespace. Typical configuration includes:

  • ACCESS_TOKEN_EXPIRE_MINUTES
  • EMAIL_RESET_TOKEN_EXPIRE_HOURS
  • PASSWORD_RESET_PATH
  • ENABLE_GOOGLE_OAUTH
  • ALLOW_GOOGLE_OAUTH_SIGNUP
  • GOOGLE_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID
  • GOOGLE_OAUTH_CLIENT_SECRET
  • GOOGLE_REDIRECT_URI

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
• If Google OAuth fails, confirm that callback URL, client ID, and secret are configured consistently.
  • If routes return authorization errors, verify that the app passes the proper get_current_account and workspace resolver dependencies.
  • If password reset flow fails, check the configured reset path and expiry values.

docs.title: Core Module
docs.text: The core package is the foundation for the entire MSFLib FastAPI monorepo. It provides configuration, database, security, event bus, policy, scope, and shared helper services that the feature modules build on.

docs.title: What it provides
docs.text:
• Namespace-aware settings and tiered config resolution
  • Database session helpers and model conventions
  • Password and JWT utilities
  • Event bus and hook registration patterns
  • Scope model for tenant/workspace/account awareness
  • Shared action and API helpers for modules

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
[tool.poetry.dependencies]
python = ">=3.10,<4.0"
msflib = { git = "https://github.com/msflib/fastapi.git", subdirectory = "core", rev = "dev" }

docs.title: Settings and config
docs.text:
The core package uses SettingsBase and ModuleSettingsBase to provide layered, namespace-aware configuration. Resolution typically follows:

default -> environment -> tenant -> workspace -> user -> request override

This is especially important for modules like workspace_config, ai_core, and downstream integrations that need scoped behavior.

docs.title: Policy layer
docs.text:
msflib.policy provides a consistent policy envelope and resolution service to resolve settings in a traceable way across scopes.

from msflib.policy import InMemoryPolicyDecisionLogger, PolicyResolutionService

docs.title: Scope model
docs.text:
The scope package gives request-scoped context for tenant, workspace, and account identities.

from msflib.scope import get_scope_dependencies

docs.title: Event bus
docs.text:
The event bus supports app-scoped emitters and listener registration so modules can react to lifecycle changes without hard-coded coupling.

from msflib.eventbus import bind_app_emitter

docs.title: Example configuration
docs.text:
from msflib.core.config import SettingsBase

class AppSettings(SettingsBase):
    SECRET_KEY: str
    DATABASE_URL: str

settings = AppSettings()

Then pull module-scoped settings using the .scope(...) pattern.

settings.scope("AUTH")
settings.scope("ACCOUNT")

docs.title: Public API surface
docs.text: Name Signature Params Returns Description SettingsBase SettingsBase environment config settings object Base app config with namespaced access ModuleSettingsBase ModuleSettingsBase module defaults settings class Base config for feature modules bind_app_emitter bind_app_emitter(app) app instance AppEmitter Bind one emitter to an app instance PolicyResolutionService PolicyResolutionService(...) scoped store, logger service Resolve policy settings with trace records get_scope_dependencies get_scope_dependencies(...) identity callables dependency namespace Build scoped auth dependencies

docs.title: Typical usage
docs.text:
from fastapi import FastAPI
from msflib.eventbus import bind_app_emitter
from msflib.scope import get_scope_dependencies

app = FastAPI()
emitter = bind_app_emitter(app)

scope_deps = get_scope_dependencies(
    get_current_account=get_current_account,
    get_current_workspace=get_current_workspace,
)

docs.title: Testing
docs.text: ./scripts/test.sh core

docs.title: Documents Module
docs.text: The Documents module provides source-agnostic document ingestion orchestration: upload, extraction, chunking, embedding, and indexing for downstream retrieval workflows.

docs.title: What it provides
docs.text:
• Direct upload document records
  • Ingestion job dispatch through msflib.ingestion
  • Source-aware extraction and indexing flow
  • Optional drivelink integration
  • Monitoring endpoints for ingestion status

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
[tool.poetry.dependencies]
msflib = { git = "https://github.com/msflib/fastapi.git", subdirectory = "core", rev = "dev" }
msflib-ai-core = { git = "https://github.com/msflib/fastapi.git", subdirectory = "modules/ai_core", rev = "dev" }
msflib-documents = { git = "https://github.com/msflib/fastapi.git", subdirectory = "modules/documents", rev = "dev" }

docs.title: Example usage
docs.text:
from fastapi import FastAPI
from msflib.documents.router import router as documents_router

app = FastAPI()
app.include_router(documents_router(prefix="/documents"))

docs.title: Public API surface
docs.text: Name Signature Params Returns Description documents_router documents_router(...) session, settings, deps router Upload and ingestion management endpoints DocumentRecord DocumentRecord document metadata model Tracks document lifecycle and source state DocumentsIngestionDispatchService DocumentsIngestionDispatchService(...) service config service Queues ingestion jobs

docs.title: Ingestion pipeline
docs.text:
The module dispatches the text_document pipeline through the shared ingestion system. The core flow is:

upload -> extract -> chunk -> embed -> index

This separates document ingestion from the host app's own transport code and keeps the job execution model consistent.

docs.title: Drivelink
docs.text: Optional lifecycle hooks can be registered when the drivelink integration is installed.

docs.title: Extraction backends
docs.text: The module relies on msflib-ai-core extraction backends and supports richer formats when optional packages are installed.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
• If file extraction fails, check whether the required extraction backend extras are installed.
  • If ingestion jobs never run, verify Redis/Broker connectivity and Celery worker startup.
  • If the API returns validation errors, confirm the upload payload and source metadata match the expected document schema.

docs.title: Ingestion Module
docs.text: The Ingestion module is the shared background job and pipeline execution layer behind the MSFLib document and knowledge flows. It centralizes queueing, retry, dead-letter handling, and pipeline registration.

docs.title: What it provides
docs.text:
• IngestionJob model and job execution state transitions
  • Celery-backed dispatch and execution flow
  • Pipeline registry and stage orchestration
  • Retry and dead-letter handling
  • Shared management API for monitoring and job control

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
[tool.poetry.dependencies]
msflib = { git = "https://github.com/msflib/fastapi.git", subdirectory = "core", rev = "dev" }
msflib-ingestion = { git = "https://github.com/msflib/fastapi.git", subdirectory = "modules/ingestion", rev = "dev" }

docs.title: Core pattern
docs.text:
The module expects a two-process setup:

  1. FastAPI process enqueues jobs
  2. Celery worker process executes jobs
from msflib.ingestion.celery import build_dispatch_task

producer = build_dispatch_task(settings)

docs.title: Public API surface
docs.text: Name Signature Params Returns Description build_celery_app build_celery_app(settings, session_factory=...) settings, session factory Celery app Builds the execution app for workers build_dispatch_task build_dispatch_task(settings) settings dispatch task Producer-side enqueue handle IngestionDispatchService IngestionDispatchService(...) task, config service Enqueues and dispatches jobs IngestionJob IngestionJob job fields model Stores job metadata and lifecycle state

docs.title: Example workflow
docs.text:
from msflib.ingestion.services.dispatch import IngestionDispatchService

service = IngestionDispatchService(task=dispatch_task)
service.enqueue_and_dispatch(
    subject_type="document",
    subject_id="abc-123",
    pipeline_kind="text_document",
    reason="new upload",
)

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
• If jobs are not processed, verify Redis connectivity and worker startup.
  • If a job fails repeatedly, inspect retry state and dead-letter entries.
  • If the worker cannot run a pipeline, confirm that the pipeline kind was registered in the worker process.

docs.title: Knowledge Module
docs.text: The Knowledge module is the knowledge-layer runtime for MSFLib. It persists canonical knowledge data, supports graph and vector projections, and exposes semantic query APIs that can be used by agents and retrieval flows.

docs.title: What it provides
docs.text:
• Canonical knowledge entities, relations, and observations
  • Scoped knowledge queries and graph/vector projections
  • Ontology-driven semantic resolution
  • Integration with the ingestion pipeline
  • Agent-aware knowledge tools for retrieval use cases

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
[tool.poetry.dependencies]
msflib = { git = "https://github.com/msflib/fastapi.git", subdirectory = "core", rev = "dev" }
msflib-ai-core = { git = "https://github.com/msflib/fastapi.git", subdirectory = "modules/ai_core", rev = "dev" }
msflib-knowledge = { git = "https://github.com/msflib/fastapi.git", subdirectory = "modules/knowledge", rev = "dev" }

docs.title: Example setup
docs.text:
from sqlmodel import Session, create_engine
from msflib.knowledge.deps import get_knowledge_dependencies

engine = create_engine("postgresql+psycopg://user:pass@host/db")
session_factory = lambda: Session(engine)

knowledge_deps = get_knowledge_dependencies(
    settings,
    session_factory=session_factory,
)

knowledge = knowledge_deps.get_knowledge_engine()

docs.text: Name Signature Params Returns Description get_knowledge_dependencies get_knowledge_dependencies(...) settings, session factory dependency namespace Builds the knowledge engine and related helpers KnowledgeEngine KnowledgeEngine(...) compiler, projections, actions engine Main query and ingest orchestration service KnowledgeCompiler KnowledgeCompiler(...) ontology compiler Converts fragments into structured stored knowledge FindEntity FindEntity(...) query params query object Entity search query FindEvidence FindEvidence(...) query params query object Evidence lookup query

docs.title: Example query
docs.text:
from msflib.knowledge.queries import FindEntity

result = knowledge.query(FindEntity(entity_type="Equipment"), scope=scope)

docs.title: Scope and governance
docs.text: Knowledge access is intentionally scoped to a tenant or workspace context. This keeps retention, data visibility, and semantic retrieval aligned with the host app's multi-tenant model.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
• If graph queries are empty, confirm that the relevant ontology and projection setup are initialized.
  • If vector search fails, verify the embeddings backend and the configured AI_CORE provider setup.
  • If ingestion is not linking to knowledge, confirm the worker process registers the knowledge pipeline kind.

docs.title: Notifications Module
docs.text: The Notifications module provides account-level notifications and admin broadcast workflows, with support for in-app delivery and optional channel dispatch such as email and SMS.

docs.title: What it provides
docs.text:
• In-app account notifications
  • Admin broadcast notifications
  • Channel dispatching by notification type and channel
  • Notification and account-notification actions

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
[tool.poetry.dependencies]
msflib = { git = "https://github.com/msflib/fastapi.git", subdirectory = "core", rev = "dev" }
msflib-notifications = { git = "https://github.com/msflib/fastapi.git", subdirectory = "modules/notifications", rev = "dev" }

Optional extras:

poetry add msflib-notifications[email]
poetry add msflib-notifications[sms]
poetry add msflib-notifications[all]

docs.title: Router wiring
docs.text:
from fastapi import FastAPI
from msflib.notifications.router import (
    account_notification_router,
    admin_account_notification_router,
)

app = FastAPI()

app.include_router(
    account_notification_router(
        get_session=get_session,
        get_current_account=get_current_account,
        prefix="/notifications",
    )
)

app.include_router(
    admin_account_notification_router(
        get_session=get_session,
        get_current_account=get_current_account,
        role_check=role_check,
        settings=settings,
        prefix="/admin/notifications",
    )
)

docs.title: Public API surface
docs.text: Name Signature Params Returns Description account_notification_router account_notification_router(...) session, account dep router User-facing notification endpoints admin_account_notification_router admin_account_notification_router(...) session, role check, settings router Admin broadcast and management endpoints dispatch_account_notifications dispatch_account_notifications(...) session, settings, data, sender, receivers notification output Sends notifications through configured channels NotificationAction NotificationAction[...] settings action instance Notification lifecycle actions

docs.title: Example: dispatch a welcome notification
docs.text:
from msflib.notifications.models import NotificationCreate, NotificationType, NotificationChannel
from msflib.notifications.service.notification import dispatch_account_notifications

notification = dispatch_account_notifications(
    session=session,
    settings=settings,
    data=NotificationCreate(
        title="Welcome",
        message="Welcome to the platform",
        channels=[NotificationChannel.inapp, NotificationChannel.email],
    ),
    n_type=NotificationType.admin,
    sender=current_admin,
    receivers=receivers,
)

docs.title: Account routes
docs.text:
• GET /notifications — list notifications
  • GET /notifications/{notification_id} — fetch one notification
  • PATCH /notifications/{notification_id}/mark — mark read/unread
  • PATCH /notifications/mark-all — mark all read/unread
  • DELETE /notifications/{notification_id} — delete one

docs.title: Admin routes
docs.text:
• POST /admin/notifications — send admin notification
  • GET /admin/notifications/all — list sent notifications
  • GET /admin/notifications/{notification_id} — fetch one sent notification
  • DELETE /admin/notifications/{notification_id} — delete one sent notification

docs.title: Channels
docs.text: Supported channels include inapp, email, sms, with enum values for push and discord as well.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
• If email or SMS channels are not working, verify the downstream email or SMS configuration and credentials.
  • If no notifications appear, confirm the notifier is passed a valid receiver list.
  • If admin routes fail, ensure the correct role check is mounted and the current account is recognized as admin.

docs.title: Workspace Config Module
docs.text: The Workspace Config module stores configuration values across tenant, workspace, and user scopes so modules can resolve effective policy and runtime behavior in a consistent way.

docs.title: What it provides
docs.text:
• Scoped configuration storage
  • Tenant/workspace/user override support
  • Request override validation patterns
  • Shared backend for policy resolution

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
[tool.poetry.dependencies]
msflib = { git = "https://github.com/msflib/fastapi.git", subdirectory = "core", rev = "dev" }
msflib-workspace_config = { git = "https://github.com/msflib/fastapi.git", subdirectory = "modules/workspace_config", rev = "dev" }

docs.title: Example usage
docs.text:
from fastapi import FastAPI
from msflib.workspace_config.router import router as workspace_config_router

app = FastAPI()

app.include_router(
    workspace_config_router(
        get_session=get_session,
        settings=settings,
        prefix="/workspace_config",
        tags=["workspace_config"],
    )
)

docs.title: Public API surface
docs.text: Name Signature Params Returns Description workspace_config_router workspace_config_router(...) session, settings router Config management routes ScopedConfigService ScopedConfigService(...) backend config service Reads/writes scoped config values ScopedConfigPolicyStoreAdapter ScopedConfigPolicyStoreAdapter(...) service adapter Adapts storage to policy resolution

docs.title: Configuration precedence
docs.text:
The module participates in a layered config model:

default -> environment -> tenant -> workspace -> user -> request override

This allows apps to set safe defaults while still letting higher-priority scopes override them.

docs.title: Example request override
docs.text:
request_override = {"overrides": {"LIMIT": 200}}

The override is validated against any allowlist defined in the module settings.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
• If values do not change as expected, confirm the scope and request override precedence is what you expect.
  • Missing config values usually mean the default is being used or the value was never persisted at the right scope.
  • If you see validation failures, ensure that override keys are allowed by the module's allowlist.

docs.title: Workspace Notifications Module
docs.text: The Workspace Notifications module adds notification flows scoped to a workspace. It is useful for apps where a user or admin needs updates tied to a specific workspace rather than a global account inbox.

docs.title: What it provides
docs.text:
• User notification endpoints
  • Admin notification endpoints for workspace-level messaging
  • Workspace-aware route wiring
  • Scoped configuration via settings.scope("WS_NOTIFICATIONS")

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
[tool.poetry.dependencies]
msflib = { git = "https://github.com/msflib/fastapi.git", subdirectory = "core", rev = "dev" }
msflib-workspace-notifications = { git = "https://github.com/msflib/fastapi.git", subdirectory = "modules/workspace_notifications", rev = "dev" }

docs.title: Router wiring
docs.text:
from fastapi import FastAPI
from msflib.workspace_notifications.router import (
    admin_user_notification_router,
    user_notification_router,
)

app = FastAPI()

app.include_router(
    user_notification_router(
        get_session=get_session,
        get_current_user=get_current_user,
        get_current_workspace=get_current_workspace,
        prefix="/workspace_notifications/user",
        tags=["workspace_notifications"],
    )
)

app.include_router(
    admin_user_notification_router(
        get_session=get_session,
        get_current_user=get_current_user,
        get_current_workspace=get_current_workspace,
        admin_role_check=admin_role_check,
        settings=settings,
        prefix="/workspace_notifications/admin",
        tags=["workspace_notifications", "admin"],
    )
)

docs.title: Public API surface
docs.text: Name Signature Params Returns Description user_notification_router user_notification_router(...) session dep, user dep, workspace dep router User-facing workspace notification routes admin_user_notification_router admin_user_notification_router(...) session dep, admin role check, workspace dep router Admin notification management routes

docs.title: Example usage
docs.text:
# list current workspace notifications
GET /workspace_notifications/user

# mark as read
PATCH /workspace_notifications/user/{notification_id}/mark

# broadcast to workspace members
POST /workspace_notifications/admin

docs.title: Settings
docs.text:
settings.scope("WS_NOTIFICATIONS")

This keeps workspace notification preferences and related behavior in the same tiered settings pattern used by the rest of the monorepo.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
• Ensure get_current_workspace is wired correctly when mounting the router.
  • Admin actions need a valid admin_role_check dependency.
  • Missing workspace membership will often cause 403 or 404 responses in these endpoints.

docs.title: Workspaces Module
docs.text: The Workspaces module handles workspace lifecycle and workspace-aware membership patterns for MSFLib applications. It is a natural companion to the account and auth modules.

docs.title: What it provides
docs.text:
• Workspace CRUD and ownership checks
  • Automatic owner membership setup
  • Workspace discovery and listing
  • Workspace logo handling
  • Workspace-aware profile routes

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
[tool.poetry.dependencies]
msflib = { git = "https://github.com/msflib/fastapi.git", subdirectory = "core", rev = "dev" }
msflib-workspaces = { git = "https://github.com/msflib/fastapi.git", subdirectory = "modules/workspaces", rev = "dev" }

docs.title: Router wiring
docs.text:
from fastapi import FastAPI
from msflib.workspaces.router import router as workspaces_router

app = FastAPI()

app.include_router(
    workspaces_router(
        get_session=get_session,
        get_current_account=get_current_account,
        get_current_account_or_none=get_current_account_or_none,
        role_check=role_check,
        settings=settings,
        prefix="/workspaces",
    )
)

docs.title: Public API surface
docs.text: Name Signature Params Returns Description workspaces_router workspaces_router(...) account deps, settings FastAPI router Handles workspace CRUD and listing user_profile_router user_profile_router(...) session, workspace, profile deps FastAPI router Exposes workspace-aware profile routes WorkspaceAction WorkspaceAction[...] settings action instance Workspace lifecycle logic UserAction UserAction[...] settings action instance Workspace membership logic

docs.title: Example: create a workspace
docs.text:
from msflib.workspaces.router import router as workspaces_router

app.include_router(workspaces_router(prefix="/workspaces"))

Then call the API:

POST /workspaces
{
  "name": "Acme Ops",
  "description": "Operations workspace",
  "status": "open"
}

docs.title: Routes
docs.text:
• GET /workspaces — list owned workspaces
  • POST /workspaces — create workspace
  • GET /workspaces/available — list available workspaces
  • GET /workspaces/{workspace_id} — fetch workspace
  • PUT /workspaces/{workspace_id} — update workspace
  • DELETE /workspaces/{workspace_id} — delete workspace

docs.title: Membership behavior
docs.text: The module resolves membership type using a priority chain so workspace ownership and role assignments remain predictable.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
• If workspace creation is rejected, confirm the account context and role check are configured.
  • If profile routes fail, confirm the workspace and current account dependencies are passed correctly.
  • If users cannot see workspaces, verify membership records are created when the workspace is created.
